    Age 6 — Iron Age

    The Rise of the Elves¶

    While other species struggled, the Elves thrived.

    They were a nature-attuned people. They did not need dwarven goods. They did not depend on the old civilization model of mines and forges and industrial supply chains. Their strength came from the land itself — forests provided shelter, rivers provided water, the soil provided food. While dwarves and humans scraped for iron, the elves built.

    Elvengar — the first great elven kingdom — was founded during this age on the continent of Kutten. The elves turned Kutten into a fortress — a bastion of elven power that no other species could breach.

    From there, they expanded. Elvengar conquered parts of the Demon Continent and West Erisdar, extending elven influence across the known world. For the first time since the Dragon Tyranny, a single species dominated Ge'or — but unlike the dragons, the elves built beauty rather than monuments to themselves.

    The Elvish Golden Age¶

    The Iron Age was also the Elvish Age. While others fought over scraps of iron, the elves created a civilization of stunning beauty:

    • Gardens — vast, intricate landscapes of flowers, trees, and winding paths, designed to be walked through for days without seeing the same view twice.
    • Mazes — living puzzles of hedgerow and stone, some of which still exist and are considered sacred sites.
    • Architecture — flowing, organic structures that seemed to grow from the ground rather than be built upon it.
    • Art — paintings, sculptures, and textiles of a quality that has never been matched. Elvish art from this era is incredibly valued in the present day. A single Age 6 elven tapestry can buy a city.

    The elves built across all of Erisdar. Their gardens, their mazes, their temples dotted every region. For a thousand years, the world was theirs.

    The Fall — The Hybrian Crash¶

    The official end of Age 6 is recorded as 3,000 BGD. The true end is 2,989 BGD.

    In that year, the Hybrian spaceship fell from the sky like a meteor and crashed in Pontus, in eastern Erisdar. The impact caused massive destruction across the eastern continent. Earthquakes. Firestorms. A plume of debris that darkened the sky.

    Refugees from eastern Erisdar flooded westward. In the chaos, human armies invaded elven territories by force, overwhelming Elvengar's defenses. The elves were pushed back to Kutten, their empire shattered, their golden age ended.

    The fall of the Hybrian ship was the single most consequential event of the age — and nobody on Ge'or knows it was a ship. The survivors saw a meteor. A fire from the sky. A divine punishment, perhaps. The truth — that it was a vessel carrying the same enemy that had consumed galaxies — would not be known for thousands of years.

    Connections¶

    [ Age 6 — The Iron Age / The Elvish Age ] ├── Span: ~4,499 to 2,989 BGD ├── Preceded By: Age 5 — Dwarf Era ├── Succeeded By: Age 8 — Age of Baoth ├── Key Event: Founding of Elvengar — the first great elven kingdom ├── Dominant Species: Elves — the Elvish Age ├── Economy: Post-Romanium poverty — iron as the downgrade replacement ├── Technology: Steam machine ruins — lost industrial knowledge ├── Elvengar Empire: Kutten fortress + conquered Demon Continent and West Erisdar ├── Legacy: Elvish art, gardens, mazes — incredibly valued today ├── End Event: Hybrian spaceship crash in Pontus (2989 BGD) ├── Consequence: Human invasions forced elves back to Kutten └── Note: No one on Ge'or knows it was a ship — they saw a meteor

    50–100 Year Transition¶

    Around 3,000 BGD, a new force rose across the continent — inexplicably, unstoppably: human empires. Frontier kingdoms that had been barely worth noticing during the dwarf and iron ages suddenly began outmaneuvering elves, demons, and dwarves alike. The Age 7 — Human Age arrived, and no one could explain why.
